name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index $4,176 per 40ft on 19 Nov after a fourth weekly fall, still above the $4,000 Alert line
state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,176 per 40ft container on 19 Nov, its fourth consecutive weekly decline but 126% above a year earlier and above the $4,000 Alert line (Drewry). Drewry expects trans-Pacific rates to fall again as carriers blank sailings, while Asia–Europe rates may rise with December peak season surcharges of $1,000–1,600 per 40ft. The next index is due on 26 Nov; a fall of about 4% would take it below the Alert line.
for_you: Importers and exporters face container costs well above a year ago, which can feed into shop prices over several months. Rates are falling on some routes but remain volatile.
rubric_hit: Alert: Drewry WCI $4,176/FEU on 19 Nov > $4,000 Alert line
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
